title: Jerarquías de legitimación del sufrimiento social: Reconocimiento, responsabilidad estatal y reparación en el estallido social chileno
abstract: The 2019 Chilean social uprising produced heterogeneous forms of victimization that were not equally recognized. This study examines how recognition of victim status, attribution of responsibility for reparation, reparation preferences and perceived lasting effects of violence vary across victimization cases, and whether ideological positioning moderates the first of these judgments. An online survey of adult residents of the Santiago Metropolitan Region (N = 5 000) randomly assigned each participant to one of five vignettes differing in type of harm, identity of the affected party and agent producing the harm. Data were analyzed with contingency tables, Cramér's V, McNemar tests and a likelihood-ratio test for the case × ideology interaction. Recognition varies across cases (40.2 % – 59.0 %; V = 0.093) and is lowest for diffuse emotional harm. Reparation preferences align with the type of harm (V = 0.199 and 0.232). Ideology moderates recognition (χ²(12) = 135.85, p < 0.001), with differences of up to 54.1 percentage points that reverse direction depending on the identity of the affected party. Perceived lasting effects of violence are high and do not vary across cases (V = 0.024). Recognition of suffering operates as a situated moral judgment.
